title: Microglia replacement by microglia transplantation (Mr MT) in the adult mouse brain
protocol: Replace endogenous microglia of the C57BL/6J mouse with gender-matched CX3CR1-CreER::DTA microglia-like cells through mr BMT.
Utilize the CX3CR1-CreER::DTA mouse as the donor for this protocol.
Turn on the orbital shaker incubator and set the temperature at 35°C and speed at 100 rpm.
Preheat the incubator for at least 20 min to 35°C.
Aliquot 4 ml of Enzyme Digestion Mix per brain into a 15 ml centrifuge tube.
Anesthetize adult CX3CR1+/GFP mouse with ketamine and xylazine.
Pinch tail to ensure deep anesthesia before transcardial perfusion.
Transcardially perfuse the donor mouse with ice-cold L15 medium + heparin until skull turns white.
Decapitate the mouse and place head in ice-cold PBS for 1 minute.
Make small lateral incisions at caudal/ventral base of skull.
Start shallow cuts from caudal/dorsal aspect moving rostrally along midline.
Cut a perpendicular “T” shape near olfactory bulbs to complete skull removal.
Use round-tip forceps to grasp and peel back dorsal halves of skull cap on both sides.
Remove dorsal halves of skull cap to expose the brain.
Harvest the brain and wash it with fresh ice-cold PBS.
Chop the brain using a razor blade on ice with 100 μL ice-cold PBS into ∼1 mm pieces.
Place the minced brain tissue into 3 mL enzyme digestion mix in a 15 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Shake the minced brain in an orbital shaker incubator at 35°C, 100 rpm for 20 min.
Terminate the digestion by adding 0.5 mL 10× papain neutralization solution.
Gently mix and sit on ice for about 1 min for tissue to settle.
Rinse the 100 μm cell strainer with DPBS and insert it into a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Transfer the supernatant above the brain chops in (A) to the 50 mL tube containing the strainer.
Add 2 mL trituration solution to the 15 mL tube containing the brain chops.
Gently triturate the brain chops 10 times with a 1 mL tip pipette.
Put on ice for about 1 min.
Repeat steps until the minced brain is diminished to about 3 mm in height.
Rinse a 100 μm cell strainer with DPBS and insert it into a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Cool the tube containing the strainer in ice.
Transfer the supernatant above the brain chops to the 50 mL tube containing the strainer.
Leave the brain chops in the original tube.
Add 2 mL trituration solution to the 15 mL tube containing the brain chops.
Gently triturate the brain chops 10 times with a 1 mL tip pipette.
Put the mixture on ice for about 1 minute.
Discard the remanence after each cycle of trituration and transfer.
Precool the centrifuge to 18°C.
Centrifuge the brain at 400 g, 18°C for 5 minutes.
Insert a 10 μL white tip on the metal pipe of the vacuum pump to aspirate the supernatant with vacuum pump suction.
Aspirate the supernatant from the brain pellet through a vacuum pump.
Add Percoll working solution to the pellet and mix gently until the pellet disappears.
Transfer the cell suspension to a new 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge the tissue at 400 g, 18°C for 20 min (set the acceleration and deceleration speed to zero).
Carefully take out the tube containing the cell pellets from the centrifuge.
Insert a 200 μL yellow tip on the metal pipe of the vacuum pump.
Aspirate the myelin debris and supernatant by the vacuum pump suction.
Add 5 mL trituration solution and wash by centrifugation at 4°C, 400 g for 5 min.
Add 10 μL anti-CD11b beads into 90 μL trituration solution.
Mix thoroughly.
Re-suspend the cell pellet with the above mixture.
Incubate the cell suspension at 4°C for 15 minutes.
Shake the cells gently every 5 minutes.
Wash the cell suspension with 5 mL MACS buffer through centrifugation at 400 g and 4°C for 5 minutes.
Re-suspend the cell pellet with 3 mL MACS buffer.
Filter the cell suspension through a 40 μm pore cell strainer.
Set up the LS column on a MACS multistand.
Wash the LS column twice with 3 mL MACS buffer.
Pour all the cell suspension into the column.
Wash the column twice with 3 mL MACS buffer.
Remove the column from the stand and insert it into a new 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 5 mL MACS buffer to the column and flush quickly using the supplied plunge.
Centrifuge at 400 g, 4°C for 10 minutes.
Re-suspend the cell pellet with 100 μL microglia resuspension solution.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 200 μL tube.
Take 1 μL out of the suspension and dilute it to 100 μL.
Count the cell number with a cell cytometer.
Clean the operation bench with 75% ethanol.
Turn on the FST hot bead sterilizer and heat the beads to about 250°C.
Insert surgical tools (fine scissors, dressing forceps, needle holders) deep into the beads for at least 20 s.
Put the sterilized surgical tools on the sterilized towel paper.
Intraperitoneally inject the recipient mouse with a mixture of ketamine (100 mg/kg) and xylazine (10 mg/kg).
After the mouse loses reflex response to toe pinching, shave the scalp hair with scissors and apply depilatory cream on the scalp.
Two minutes later, clean the scalp with water.
Fix the mouse head on a stereotactic apparatus.
Apply iodophor on the scalp with a cotton swab and cut the scalp by scissors to expose the skull.
Use cotton swab to remove the mucosa over the skull until the skull gets dry.
Mark the location on the skull at −2.00 mm AP and −1.5 mm ML with an 18 G needle.
Moisten the skull surface with DPBS.
Use a microdrill with a 0.6 mm bore bit to open a dimple at the marked location using the drill speed at 200 rpm.
Carefully remove the thinned skull piece and the underneath dura in the dimple with a 27 G needle.
Centrifuge concentrated microglia suspension at 100 g for 1 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Calculate the amount of microglia resuspension solution using a cell counter, ensuring the remaining volume is less than 5 μL.
Control the cell concentration to 1 × 10^5 cells per μL.
Aspirate 0.8 μL concentrated cell suspension into a pre-cooled 5 μL Hamilton syringe equipped with a 30 G needle.
Attach the syringe on a micro-pump and set injection amount at 0.3 μL; injection speed at 3 min.
Connect the syringe to the pump onto the arm of the stereotactic apparatus.
Move the syringe needle close to the small window on the skull.
Insert the needle to −1.5 mm depth.
Start the injection process and infuse 0.3 μL microglia cell suspension at this depth.
Withdraw the needle slightly, then insert it to −0.7 mm depth.
Infuse another 0.3 μL microglia cell suspension at this new depth.
Hold the needle in place for 1 min after the second infusion.
Slowly withdraw the needle at a rate of about 0.02 mm/s.
Moisten the skull and the scalp with DPBS.
Close the scalp together with 4 to 5 sutures, 3 mm apart.
Sterilize the suture with iodophor.
Apply erythromycin ointment on the wound.
Intraperitoneally inject 0.5 mL sterilized saline to the mouse.
Put the mouse into a cage laid with sterilized towel paper.
Place the cage on a heating pad set at 45°C.
Add moistened chows near the mouse.
Dissolve neomycin in drinking water (1.1 g/L).
Wait until the mice recover from anesthesia.
Inject meloxicam (1 mg/kg, dissolved in saline) intraperitoneally.
Put the cage back to the animal facility.
Inject meloxicam (1 mg/kg) intraperitoneally every 12 hours for the first 2 days after surgery.
Change the bedding materials every day and keep the cage clean.
Feed the mouse with tamoxifen-formulated chow diet ad libitum for 30 days.
